notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 18 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1828cont), the 26 weekly issues from 3 July to 25 December 1918, a quiet wartime half-year. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1917-1920, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1918. The labels are printed with a row of leader dots ('Owner........'), which extract.py reads since the January to June 1919 volume. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; most of the 53 rows read needed a name, a cost or the wording corrected, and a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out. Entries cut by a column break were read on in the next column. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or engineer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's premises that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays. The dated running heads in this volume are stale type (one says 6 November on six issues), so issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue; issues.py missed four covers, which were set by hand from the cover or from the masthead two or four leaves after it). One single house that was read against the image and has no name left to publish sits with the held single houses. Two held houses (August 1918 in this volume, November 1919 in vol. 19 pt. 2) whose parcels got a page from this volume were read against the image and stay held because the roll gives apartments or flats there. One contract (Shotwell north of 19th) sits on a parcel with no sf-eas-addresses row and is logged unresolved.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 18 pt. 2 to 31 read (July 1918 to January 1932); the 7 half-year volumes before July 1918 (1915 to June 1918) are unread, buildingengineer1818cont (January to June 1918) next. In this volume: 31 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but two still need the image check). 133 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 345 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 1,264 numbered entries read, 561 San Francisco rows, 216 placed on a parcel, 53 picked and read against the page image, 36 published on 34 pages (11 seeded), 15 held back: six alterations with nothing to confirm the street number, seven storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, one piece of minor work and one misread street; one more joined the held houses and one sits on a parcel with no address row.
